carveOutsConsidered: common automated-tool finding without H/M path

checks.reasoning: The trigger is a hostile-or-broken registered token, which superficially reads as 'weird ERC20'. The carve-out does NOT apply for two reasons. (1) The carve-out exists because a protocol cannot be expected to support ARBITRARY tokens; Antimatter's stablecoin set is an owner-curated allowlist, so no arbitrary-token assumption is being imposed. (2) The root cause is caller-side and token-independent: an unbounded RETURNDATACOPY with unmetered gas forwarding at :292, a recognised defect class in its own right, present regardless of which token is registered.

Registration-GATED, not owner-CAUSED. Registering a stablecoin is the intended operation; the hostile return shape appears afterwards via a proxy implementation change, outside the owner's control. The sanitizer's ruling is UPHELD.
Not tool-sourced. CODE-203 reasoning plus a measured PoC; no SAST engine reported it.

findings.notes: Valid, but its honest weight is defence-in-depth and the classifier already says so. The marginal-capability argument (a token that can do this can already brick its own pair by reverting transferFrom) is correct and must stay in the write-up so the Low is not read as understated.
findings.recommendation: Keep as filed in the QA bundle.

checks.reasoning: CARVE-OUT DECLINED after explicit reasoning rather than label-matching. decimals() is an OPTIONAL part of EIP-20 ('OPTIONAL - may be omitted'), so a token without it (T2) is STANDARD-CONFORMANT, not weird. T3's token is stronger still: it implements decimals(), answers 18, and is registered as 18 - its answer is CORRECT and matches. Nothing about its transfer, approve or balance semantics is non-standard. Calling it a weird token would stretch the carve-out to cover a token that is right about everything the protocol asked it, which would apply the list too broadly. The design also self-refutes the carve-out: PhusdStableMinter carries an explicit registered `decimals` field precisely because the protocol does not want to depend on token self-report.

checks.evidence: story-002 (Why not try/catch, lines 129-160) enumerates 'empty return data (a token with a permissive fallback and no decimals())', 'an address with no code', and a reverting decimals(), and states 'Both approaches fail closed, which is the security property.' T1 (decimals() dropped/reverting) and T2 (never had decimals()) are therefore SPONSOR-INTENDED fail-closed behaviour, considered and chosen on the record.
checks.reasoning: Reporting T1/T2 as defects flags intended design as a bug. T3 is NOT covered: the story never considers a decimals() that is non-view, and the failure there is not the staticcall at all - toStableAmount is declared `public view`, so a state-mutating decimals() would fail identically under try/catch. That is an unconsidered case and is the finding's real content.
Sanitizer ruling UPHELD and strengthened. T3 involves no owner error whatsoever: the registration is correct, the registered value matches the token's own answer, and the call still reverts.

findings.narrowerFraming: File L-05 on TWO legs only: (a) T3 - an honest, correctly-registered token whose decimals() is not view-callable is rejected although its answer matches (PoC-proven); (b) the DETECTION ASYMMETRY - PhusdStableMinter.mint keeps working for the same token because it reads only config.decimals, so mint-path monitoring shows the protocol healthy while the antimatter path is dead. Reframe T1/T2 from 'triggers' to 'documented, intended fail-closed cases (story-002)' and cite them as context for the registration checklist, not as defects. Doing this does NOT weaken the finding: T3 is the trigger the classifier itself calls 'the one that matters' and is the only one carrying an honest-token argument.
findings.law1Caution: THE PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION IS UNSAFE AS WRITTEN AND MUST NOT SHIP UNQUALIFIED. 'Treat an UNAVAILABLE decimals() as no independent confirmation and fall back to the minter's registered value' re-opens exactly the fail-OPEN path that M-01 (a1c81428a47ad295, fix-pending) exists to close, for every token that can make its decimals() unavailable - which a lying token controls. Story-002 chose fail-closed deliberately and called it 'the security property'. Promote the ALTERNATIVE (cross-check once at registration/acceptance time on Antimatter's side and cache it) to primary: it fixes T3 without reintroducing any fail-open branch. Reversing a story-sanctioned security property must be raised as a decision for the owner, never slipped in as a mitigation line.
findings.recommendation: Keep in the QA bundle, rescoped to (a)+(b), with the recommendation reordered. The borderline flag and the severity-auditor referral are unaffected by this validity ruling - rescoping does not change the band, since T3 is the leg the Low already rests on.

carveOutsConsidered: speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause

checks.reasoning: CARVE-OUT DECLINED. The claim is present-tense and demonstrated, verified independently this session: Antimatter.sol:234 calls minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount); PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 calls calculateMintAmount(stablecoin, amount) with the same arguments, in the same transaction, against the same config storage; calculateMintAmount is `public view` and pure over that storage. No hypothetical future minter is required for the defect. The FUTURE minter appears only in the finding's own 'assumptions' as a reason the check retains residual value - i.e. it argues AGAINST the finding, not for it, which is the opposite of speculation.

In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority on this project, and falsely-exhaustive docs raise rather than lower severity. The operational value is the false-closure block on F-01, which is a Law-1 protection, not a style note.
The defective comment and error name are in src/Antimatter.sol:232-233/:257. The minter is read-only context.

findings.narrowerFraming: ACCURACY DEFECT IN THE FINDING ITSELF - must be corrected before it reaches the QA bundle. 'The check is a tautology' is NOT strictly true and the run's own evidence disproves it. mintedForStable is a BALANCE DELTA (phUSD balance after minus before), not the minter's return value, so the equality also fires when third-party phUSD arrives mid-call - proven by Tier2Delta.t.sol::test_midCallPhUSDInjectionNowReverts, which reverts PhUSDAmountMismatch(100e18, 100e18+1). The check therefore genuinely closes ledger L-01's donation-attribution gap. Restate the finding as: 'the check verifies the minter against its own quote and rejects mid-call phUSD injection, but it is NOT a slippage or minimum-output guard - both sides re-quote at whatever rate is live at execution, so an owner rate change mid-flight passes the check - yet the comment at :232-233 and the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch read as protection against being short-changed.' The false-closure block on F-01 survives this rewording intact and is unaffected.
findings.notes: Rescoping is mandatory, not stylistic: 'tautology / no-op on 100% of the honest path' overstates in the direction of dismissing working protection, and the pipeline rejects claims a reader can falsify from the repo's own test file.
findings.recommendation: Keep at QA in the QA bundle with the corrected framing. Reproduce falseClosureBlock verbatim wherever F-01 is referenced.
